title: You’ve heard about the Tree of Life.
paragraphs: You’ve heard about the Tree of Life.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
It was never just a tree.
It was access.
THE FIRST MENTION — AND THE FIRST LOSS
In the beginning, the Tree of Life stood in the middle of the garden.
“The LORD God made all kinds of trees grow out of the ground… and the tree of life in the middle of the garden…” — Genesis 2:9
It represented something humanity once had without fear:
Unbroken, eternal life in the presence of God.

No death.
No shame.
No separation.
But then…

You chose independence.
Sin entered.
Everything fractured.
And God did something that feels harsh—until you understand it:
“He drove out the man… to guard the way to the tree of life.” — Genesis 3:24
God blocked access.
Not out of cruelty…
But mercy.
Because eternal life in a fallen state would mean eternal separation, eternal corruption, eternal decay.

God saw it.
You were no longer fit to live forever like that.
WHAT THE TREE OF LIFE REPRESENTS NOW
Fast forward.
The Tree of Life shows up again—but not in a garden.
In a promise.
“To the one who is victorious, I will give the right to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God.” — Revelation 2:7
Now it represents something deeper:
Restored access to God through Jesus Christ.
Not physical fruit.
Spiritual life. Eternal life. Redemption.
Because the real problem was never hunger…
It was sin.
THE SHIFT YOU MISSED
You don’t get back to the Tree of Life by trying harder.
You don’t earn your way back into the garden.
You can’t fix what broke in you.
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
That’s the diagnosis.
Death isn’t just physical.
It’s separation from God.
And you’ve felt it.

That emptiness.
That restlessness.
That quiet fear when everything slows down.
You knew.
THEN JESUS ENTERED THE STORY
The Tree of Life is no longer a location.
It’s a Person.
“I am the way and the truth and the life…” — John 14:6
Read that again.
The life.
Jesus didn’t just point to life.
He is life.
And the cross?
It looked like death…
But it functioned like a tree.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
The same place where sin once separated you from life…
became the place where Jesus absorbed your sin to bring you back.
WHAT THE TREE OF LIFE REPRESENTS TODAY
Right now, today, the Tree of Life represents:
A choice.
Not in a garden.
In your heart.
You are either:

• Still cut off — living, but spiritually dead
• Or restored — alive through Christ
There is no middle ground.
THE FINAL PICTURE
The story ends where it began—but transformed:
“On each side of the river stood the tree of life… and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.” — Revelation 22:2
Access is restored.
Death is gone.
Separation is finished.
But only for those who came through Jesus.
DECISION MOMENT
You don’t need to find a tree.
You need to face the truth.

You’ve sinned.
You’ve been separated.
You cannot fix it yourself.
But grace is standing in front of you.
“…but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
Not earned.
Given.
WHAT WILL YOU DO WITH THAT?
Reject it—and remain cut off.
Receive it—and live.

No delay.
No excuses.
No pretending.
This is your moment.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
